title: Aviation mechanic maintenance and inspection records practice questions
description: Practice questions on 14 CFR Part 43 records: overhauled and rebuilt, 43.9 and 43.11 entries, life-limited parts and FAA Form 337.

questions.question: Under 43.2(a)(1), what must have been done to a component part, using methods, techniques, and practices acceptable to the Administrator, before a required maintenance entry may describe it as overhauled?

options.A: It has been inspected and functionally checked while installed
options.B: It has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary, and reassembled
options.C: It has been fitted with new parts only and run for a set break-in period
options.D: It has been cleaned and visually inspected for damage

questions.explanation: 43.2(a)(1) requires that "Using methods, techniques, and practices acceptable to the Administrator, it has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary, and reassembled"; it must also have been tested under 43.2(a)(2).

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.2, Records of overhaul and rebuilding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Using methods, techniques, and practices acceptable to the Administrator, it has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary, and reassembled

questions.question: A shop wants to describe an engine as "rebuilt" in a required maintenance entry. To what does 43.2(b) say the engine must have been tested?

options.A: The service limits in the current maintenance manual
options.B: Limits agreed between the shop and the aircraft owner
options.C: The limits in the most recent airworthiness directive
options.D: The same tolerances and limits as a new item

questions.explanation: An item may be described as rebuilt only if it has been "disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary, reassembled, and tested to the same tolerances and limits as a new item".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.2, Records of overhaul and rebuilding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: reassembled, and tested to the same tolerances and limits as a new item

questions.question: Which parts does 43.2(b) allow in an item described as rebuilt?

options.A: New parts, or used parts that conform to new part tolerances and limits or to approved oversized or undersized dimensions
options.B: New parts only
options.C: Used parts that are within the manufacturer's service limits
options.D: Any parts the person approving the work considers serviceable

questions.explanation: 43.2(b) requires the work to be done "using either new parts or used parts that either conform to new part tolerances and limits or to approved oversized or undersized dimensions."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.2, Records of overhaul and rebuilding (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: using either new parts or used parts that either conform to new part tolerances and limits or to approved oversized or undersized dimensions.

questions.question: Under 43.9(a)(1), the maintenance record entry describes the work performed. What does the rule accept in place of that description?

options.A: A reference to the aircraft's total time in service
options.B: A copy of the owner's purchase order
options.C: A reference to data acceptable to the Administrator
options.D: The phrase "work completed per owner request"

questions.explanation: 43.9(a)(1) calls for "A description (or reference to data acceptable to the Administrator) of work performed."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: A description (or reference to data acceptable to the Administrator) of work performed.

questions.question: A mechanic approves work that another person performed under the mechanic's supervision. Under 43.9(a)(3), whose name must the entry include besides the approving person's signature?

options.A: The name of the person who performed the work
options.B: The name of the aircraft owner
options.C: The name of the FAA inspector for the area
options.D: The name of the parts supplier

questions.explanation: 43.9(a)(3) requires "The name of the person performing the work if other than the person specified in paragraph (a)(4) of this section", which is the person approving the work.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The name of the person performing the work if other than the person specified in paragraph (a)(4) of this section.

questions.question: Under 43.9(a)(4), what does the signature of the person approving the work constitute?

options.A: Approval for return to service of the whole aircraft
options.B: A certification that the aircraft is in airworthy condition
options.C: The approval for return to service only for the work performed
options.D: Acceptance of the work by the aircraft owner

questions.explanation: 43.9(a)(4) states: "The signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The signature constitutes the approval for return to service only for the work performed.

questions.question: Under 43.9(d), in addition to the 43.9(a) entry, who enters a major repair or major alteration on a form and disposes of the form in the manner prescribed in appendix B?

options.A: The aircraft owner
options.B: The operator's chief pilot
options.C: The FAA Aircraft Registration Branch
options.D: The person performing the work

questions.explanation: 43.9(d) says "major repairs and major alterations shall be entered on a form, and the form disposed of, in the manner prescribed in appendix B, by the person performing the work."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.9, Content, form, and disposition of maintenance, preventive maintenance, rebuilding, and alteration records (except inspections performed in accordance with part 91, part 125, § 135.411(a)(1), and § 135.419 of this chapter) (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: major repairs and major alterations shall be entered on a form, and the form disposed of, in the manner prescribed in appendix B, by the person performing the work.

questions.question: How does 43.10(a) define a life-limited part?

options.A: Any part that has been installed for more than half of its expected service life
options.B: Any part for which a mandatory replacement limit is specified in the type design, the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness, or the maintenance manual
options.C: Any part listed in an airworthiness directive
options.D: Any part that the owner chooses to track by hours or cycles

questions.explanation: "Life-limited part means any part for which a mandatory replacement limit is specified in the type design, the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness, or the maintenance manual."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Life-limited part means any part for which a mandatory replacement limit is specified in the type design, the Instructions for Continued Airworthiness, or the maintenance manual.

questions.question: A life-limited part is temporarily removed and reinstalled to perform maintenance. Its life status has not changed, and the product does not accumulate time in service while it is removed. Under 43.10(b), what further condition must be met for no 43.10(c) disposition to be required?

options.A: The part is reinstalled by the same person who removed it
options.B: The removal and reinstallation is performed on the same serial numbered product
options.C: The part is reinstalled on the same calendar day
options.D: The removal is reported on FAA Form 337

questions.explanation: No disposition is required if the life status has not changed, "The removal and reinstallation is performed on the same serial numbered product", and the product "does not accumulate time in service while the part is removed."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The removal and reinstallation is performed on the same serial numbered product; and

questions.question: If a removed life-limited part is controlled by mutilation under 43.10(c)(6), what must the mutilation do?

options.A: Render the part beyond repair and incapable of being reworked to appear to be airworthy
options.B: Remove the part number so it cannot be traced
options.C: Mark the part with its current life status
options.D: Reduce the part to a size that fits a scrap bin

questions.explanation: 43.10(c)(6) states: "The mutilation must render the part beyond repair and incapable of being reworked to appear to be airworthy."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The mutilation must render the part beyond repair and incapable of being reworked to appear to be airworthy.

questions.question: A person removes a life-limited part from a type certificated product and later sells it without mutilating it. What does 43.10(d) require to go with the part?

options.A: A new FAA Form 337
options.B: A copy of the selling person's mechanic certificate
options.C: Only the sales invoice
options.D: The mark, tag, or other record used to comply with 43.10

questions.explanation: The person "must transfer with the part the mark, tag, or other record used to comply with this section, unless the part is mutilated before it is sold or transferred."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.10, Disposition of life-limited aircraft parts (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must transfer with the part the mark, tag, or other record used to comply with this section, unless the part is mutilated before it is sold or transferred.

questions.question: Besides the type of inspection and a brief description of its extent, what does 43.11(a)(2) require an inspection entry to contain?

options.A: The date of the inspection and the time remaining until the next inspection
options.B: The names of everyone who assisted with the inspection
options.C: The date of the inspection and aircraft total time in service
options.D: The engine time since its last overhaul

questions.explanation: 43.11(a)(2) requires "The date of the inspection and aircraft total time in service."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The date of the inspection and aircraft total time in service.

questions.question: After an inspection that is not a progressive inspection, an aircraft is not approved for return to service because of needed maintenance. Under 43.11(a)(5), the entry's statement says a dated list of discrepancies and unairworthy items has been provided for whom?

options.A: The local FAA office
options.B: The next mechanic who works on the aircraft
options.C: The aircraft owner or operator
options.D: The aircraft manufacturer

questions.explanation: The statement ends: "a list of discrepancies and unairworthy items dated (date) has been provided for the aircraft owner or operator."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: a list of discrepancies and unairworthy items dated (date) has been provided for the aircraft owner or operator.

questions.question: If an inspection is conducted under an inspection program provided for in part 91, 125, or § 135.411(a)(1), what must the 43.11(a)(7) entry identify?

options.A: The inspection program and that part of the inspection program accomplished
options.B: The inspector's employer and the hourly rate charged
options.C: Only the date the program was first approved
options.D: The aircraft's next scheduled annual inspection date

questions.explanation: The entry "must identify the inspection program, that part of the inspection program accomplished, and contain a statement that the inspection was performed in accordance with the inspections and procedures for that particular program."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: the entry must identify the inspection program, that part of the inspection program accomplished, and contain a statement that the inspection was performed in accordance with the inspections and procedures for that particular program.

questions.question: During an inspection required by part 91, the person performing it finds the aircraft unairworthy. Under 43.11(b), what must that person give the owner or lessee?

options.A: A completed FAA Form 337
options.B: A signed and dated list of those discrepancies
options.C: A maintenance release
options.D: A copy of the aircraft's type certificate data sheet

questions.explanation: The person "must give the owner or lessee a signed and dated list of those discrepancies."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must give the owner or lessee a signed and dated list of those discrepancies.

questions.question: For items permitted to be inoperative under § 91.213(d)(2), where does 43.11(b) say the person performing the inspection places a placard marking it "Inoperative"?

options.A: Only on the aircraft's entry door
options.B: On the cover of the aircraft maintenance record
options.C: Next to the aircraft's airworthiness certificate
options.D: On each inoperative instrument and the cockpit control of each item of inoperative equipment

questions.explanation: That person "shall place a placard, that meets the aircraft's airworthiness certification regulations, on each inoperative instrument and the cockpit control of each item of inoperative equipment".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 43.11, Content, form, and disposition of records for inspections conducted under parts 91 and 125 and §§ 135.411(a)(1) and 135.419 of this chapter (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: on each inoperative instrument and the cockpit control of each item of inoperative equipment

questions.question: Under Appendix B(a)(3) to Part 43, where is a copy of the FAA Form 337 forwarded, and by when?

options.A: To the FAA Aircraft Registration Branch in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, within 48 hours after the item is approved for return to service
options.B: To the aircraft manufacturer, within 48 hours after the work begins
options.C: To the nearest FAA office, before the next flight
options.D: To the aircraft's insurer, within 30 days after the work is completed

questions.explanation: The person shall "Forward a copy of that form to the FAA Aircraft Registration Branch in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, within 48 hours after the aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, or appliance is approved for return to service."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix B—Recording of Major Repairs and Major Alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Forward a copy of that form to the FAA Aircraft Registration Branch in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, within 48 hours after the aircraft, airframe, aircraft engine, propeller, or appliance is approved for return to service.

questions.question: A certificated repair station uses the customer's work order for a major repair under Appendix B(b). What retention period does Appendix B(b)(2) set for its duplicate copy of the work order?

options.A: 30 days from the date of the repair
options.B: 90 days from the date of approval for return to service
options.C: One year from the date of approval for return to service
options.D: At least two years from the date of approval for return to service

questions.explanation: The repair station must "retain a duplicate copy for at least two years from the date of approval for return to service".

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix B—Recording of Major Repairs and Major Alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: retain a duplicate copy for at least two years from the date of approval for return to service

questions.question: Under Appendix B(c), for a major repair or major alteration made by a person authorized in § 43.17, who executes the FAA Form 337?

options.A: Only the aircraft owner
options.B: Only a certificated repair station
options.C: The person who performs the work and the person authorized by § 43.17 to approve that work
options.D: The FAA Aircraft Registration Branch

questions.explanation: "the person who performs the major repair or major alteration and the person authorized by § 43.17 to approve that work shall execute an FAA Form 337 at least in duplicate."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix B—Recording of Major Repairs and Major Alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: the person who performs the major repair or major alteration and the person authorized by § 43.17 to approve that work shall execute an FAA Form 337 at least in duplicate.

questions.question: For an extended-range fuel tank installed within the passenger compartment, Appendix B(d) requires FAA Form 337 in at least triplicate. Besides giving a copy to the owner and forwarding one to the FAA, what is done with a completed copy?

options.A: It is kept by the person who performed the work for two years
options.B: It is placed on board the aircraft as specified in § 91.417
options.C: It is sent to the fuel tank manufacturer
options.D: It is posted in the cockpit next to the fuel selector

questions.explanation: A completed copy shall be "Placed on board the aircraft as specified in § 91.417 of this chapter", given to the owner, and forwarded to the FAA Aircraft Registration Branch.

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR Part 43, Appendix B—Recording of Major Repairs and Major Alterations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Placed on board the aircraft as specified in § 91.417 of this chapter;
